metadata.name: session.put
metadata.description: (state, name, tokens) - store a service's live session tokens ({ access, refresh?, exp?, meta? }; tokens may be an object or a JSON string) in the module-scope token store, and write a non-secret session.<name>.status cel ({ status: active, exp }) that formulas react to. The tokens NEVER become a cel value and NEVER enter an archive — only the status does. Called by auth providers (e.g. supabase-auth) on sign-in, not by user formulas. Once the wallet is unlocked, the REFRESH token also persists to an ECDH-wrapped OPFS sidecar (session-token-persistence): unlocking the wallet on the next boot restores it via session.restore.

metadata.name: session.handle
metadata.description: (state, name, kind?) - mint a SecretHandle for a service's access token (kind='access', default) or refresh token (kind='refresh'). The handle carries the name + a resolver closure over the module-scope store; it dehydrates to name-only (the resolver, and the token, are dropped). Effect sites (e.g. the supabase data verb) resolve() the access handle to set the Authorization bearer; an auth provider resolves the refresh handle to rotate the access token. The token is never surfaced as a cel value.

metadata.name: session.peek
metadata.description: (state, name) - return the non-secret status snapshot for a service ({ status: active|none, exp, hasRefresh }). Mirrors the session.<name>.status cel; never returns the token.

metadata.name: session.forget
metadata.description: (state, name) - drop a service's tokens from the store (sign-out) and set session.<name>.status to { status: none }. After this the handle's resolver returns undefined.

metadata.name: session.restore
metadata.description: (state) -> restored names[]. After keystore.unlock: unwrap every wallet-wrapped refresh-token sidecar (/plastron/session/<name>.tok) back into the module-scope Map (refresh only - no access claim, no status write) and return the names; the caller fans out to each provider's refresh op (e.g. supabase.auth refresh) to mint fresh access tokens. Names already live in the Map are skipped; a sidecar the current wallet can't unwrap is left in place.

metadata.name: session.persist
metadata.description: (state) -> persisted names[]. Re-wrap every LIVE session's refresh token under the (now-unlocked) wallet into its OPFS sidecar - covers sign-ins that happened while the wallet was locked or absent. session.put persists automatically once the wallet is unlocked; session.forget deletes the sidecar.
